built.summary:
I built the pure part of U33a: the consent-basis catalogue and its test section. Nothing was run (no node, tsx or tsc). I checked the code by reading it against the real types, and byte-scanned all three files: no control characters, zero-width characters or no-break spaces.

**The catalogue, `src/lib/marketing/consent-basis.ts`.** It imports nothing, so a browser screen can use it.
- **The four bases:** OWN_FORM, OWN_EVENT and AGENT_ROSTER are first-party. THIRD_PARTY (a bought list) is the only one that is not, and it produces no consent wording. The four wordings and ADULT_ATTESTATION_WORDING ("They told us they are 18 or older.") are copied word for word from the U33 spec drafts.
- **Marked as G4 drafts in code:**
  - `CONSENT_BASIS_G4 = { state: "DRAFT", confirmedOn: null }`.
  - Every `since` is `UNSHIPPED` ("unshipped"), so no draft claims a ship date.
  - The file header says nothing writes these wordings until Ali confirms them.
  - The "APPEND BELOW THIS LINE" marker is there.
- **Exports (the spec's API):** THIRD_PARTY_NOTICE, PROOF_NOTE_MIN = 10, PROOF_NOTE_MAX = 500, consentBasisFor, importConsentWording, isAttestedImportWording, isImportAttestation, checkConsentBasisInput and importConsentEvidence.
- **Small additions beyond the spec:**
  - `CONSENT_BASIS_REFUSAL_SENTENCE`: one sentence per refusal, so the panel and the server action say the same thing.
  - `normalizeProofNote` and `proofNoteChars`, for the panel's live character count.
  - `ImportAttestationRow`, so the file needs no server type.
- **Behaviour:**
  - `importConsentWording` builds the wording from the catalogue's own entry. A look-alike basis object produces null, so every stored wording is one the attestation check recognises.
  - `checkConsentBasisInput` refuses, in this order: unknown basis, phone number in the note, note too short, note too long, 18+ box not ticked.
  - The phone screen refuses any run of 9 or more digits once spaces, dots, dashes, brackets and `+` are removed. It also catches full-width digits, zero-width characters and en dashes.
  - Only the boolean `true` counts as the 18+ tick. A tick left over from a first-party choice is never carried onto a bought list.
  - The function never throws on a malformed request; it refuses instead.

**The test section, `scripts/marketing-consent/consent-basis.mts`.** It has 19 assertions and 18 red cases, all in memory.
- **Assertions:**
  - **Pin:** a sha of the entries plus the 18+ sentence equals `PINNED_BASIS_SHA = "f9d9ac400b285144"`, over the first 4 entries. I computed it with Python from the file's bytes.
  - **Catalogue:** keys match exactly as spelled; exactly one basis is not consent; each composed wording names 50pick, offers, news, SMS and 18; the import wordings never overlap the player's SMS sentences; the bought-list notice says the right things.
  - **Attestation check:** composed wordings pass and look-alikes do not; a ledger row counts only if it is GIVEN, from IMPORT, signed by an officer and under an attested wording.
  - **Input check (in1–in8):** each refusal, the 10 and 500 character limits, the phone screen variants, the 18+ rules, and the malformed-request cases.
  - **Evidence:** `import:<run> basis:<KEY> note:<note>` on one line.
  - **draft1:** while DRAFT, every `since` reads "unshipped"; once confirmed, every `since` is a real date on or after the confirmation.
  - **draft2:** while DRAFT, no src file that writes a ledger row or a run's basis imports the catalogue. It walks the real src tree, prints how many files it read, requires at least 1000, and requires that it finds at least 3 ledger writers so the walk is known to work.
- **`--prove-red`:** first the shipped code must pass, then the defect-free model must pass, then each red case must fail on its own named assertion. The red cases cover the spec's plants (one character of OWN_FORM changed, AGENT_ROSTER removed, THIRD_PARTY flagged first-party, digit screen removed, 18+ ignored) plus entries reordered, draft-date mistakes, the G4 guard, and the rest.

**Registration.** I hooked the section into `scripts/marketing-consent.test.mts` myself, in both modes, with the tally updated. That file was not on the do-not-edit list, and the diff is 28 lines added and 3 changed. `test:marketing-consent` is already in predeploy, so no package.json change is needed.

**One edit for you to make in `scripts/client-graph-safe.test.mjs`** (I was not allowed to touch it). Add this to PINNED, after `"lib/marketing/footer.ts",`:
```
    // ⭐ ADDED 2026-10-01 (U33a). The import consent-basis catalogue: the basis panel (U33b) renders it in the browser, while the gate (consent.ts) and the import writer read it on the server. It imports nothing.
    "lib/marketing/consent-basis.ts",
```
howToVerify: npm run typecheck — consent-basis.ts sits under src/, so tsc covers it. The .mts section is not typechecked; it was written to strict TS anyway.
npm run test:marketing-consent — the U33a block should print 19 PASS lines, U33.pin through U33.draft2. U33.draft2's detail should read about 'walked ~1200 src files · 4 wording writer(s) · DRAFT'.

npm run red:marketing-consent — expect '§0 basis baseline · consent-basis.ts: 19 passed, 0 failed', then '§0b basis model · no defect set: 19 passed', then 'basis 18/18' and RED PROOF COMPLETE. No 'basis plant … changed nothing' problems should appear.

If U33.pin fails at baseline with the catalogue unchanged, my outside-node sha is wrong. The formula is sha256 over [key|since|String(firstParty)|wording for the first 4 entries, then ADULT_ATTESTATION_WORDING] joined by newlines, utf8, first 16 hex characters. Re-derive it with node and compare it to the printed sha before re-pinning.
After adding the PINNED line to scripts/client-graph-safe.test.mjs, run npm run test:client-graph-safe — consent-basis.ts must come out clean (it has no imports).
npm run test:dal-parity — 20.0 should be unchanged: no new db.messagingConsent.create( caller. The header comment that mentions it is removed before the scan.
npm run test:red-anchors — §4: the marketing-consent harness and the new section still make no file-writing call.
Byte check (already run): no control characters, zero-width characters or no-break spaces in consent-basis.ts, consent-basis.mts or the runner edit; the regex escapes appear as written in the source.
openQuestions: U33.draft2 (the G4 guard) will turn red when U33a's engine commit adds import-consent.ts, a ledger writer that imports the catalogue, unless Ali has answered G4 first. That follows DECISIONS-U29-U40 ('the build stops at each' owner gate), but it stops the build at the writer's code rather than at its first caller, which is U32's batch action. If you want the writer to land, uncalled, before G4, narrow draft2's writer pattern to callers of recordImportConsentBatch.

When Ali confirms G4, four things change together: set CONSENT_BASIS_G4 = { state: 'CONFIRMED', confirmedOn: '<day>' }; replace every UNSHIPPED since with the ship date of the deploy that can first write it; re-take PINNED_BASIS_SHA once; and record it in COMPLIANCE-DECISIONS. U33.draft1 fails until the since dates are set.

The radio-card labels are mine, not the spec's: 'Our own form', 'A 50pick event or shop', 'A registered 50pick agent', 'A bought or third-party list'. They are admin wording only, never stored and not pinned.
For Ali at G4: the AGENT_ROSTER draft says 'agreed to receive', without the 'there' the other two have. I kept it word for word from the spec.
I check for a phone number before checking length (the spec lists length first). A short note that is just a phone number therefore says 'Remove the phone number' rather than 'too short'.

The spec's own owner-decision 1 says 'ship as drafted' if Ali doesn't answer. DECISIONS-U29-U40 G4 says the build stops instead, and I followed DECISIONS. The docs agent should note that override wherever §9 U33 is rewritten.

findings.problem: U33.draft2 stops the build at the wrong step. It fails as soon as any src file that calls db.messagingConsent.create( (or db.contactImport.fixConsentBasis() names consent-basis while the gate is DRAFT. U33a's engine commit (critic step 8) adds import-consent.ts, which does both, so that commit cannot land until Ali answers G4. The same commit carries the consent.ts gate rewrite, the optout fixture and the §20 WRITERS entry. X3 then makes U33's consent write part of U32's commitBatch (step 10), so the whole import track waits on G4, and Ali is away. The real risk is the first row written in production, and that cannot happen before the first production-reachable caller exists: X16 says *Actions ship only with their UI (steps 9/10). The module's own header (lines 9-10) also says U33.w*/g* 'arrive with U33a's engine commit', which draft2 forbids. DECISIONS G4 ('the build stops') supports either reading, so this needs an explicit call from the lead, not a silent stall.
findings.fix: Lead decides, and the result is recorded as a numbered point in plan §0h. Option A (recommended): narrow draft2 so that, while DRAFT, nothing production-reachable reaches the catalogue. That means no file under src/app and no "use server" module that imports import-consent / consent-basis or calls recordImportConsentBatch( / fixConsentBasis(. The uncalled writer and its in-memory tests can then land at step 8, and steps 9/10 still stop at G4. Option B: keep it as written and state in §0/§0h that critic step 8 waits for G4. Either way, rewrite the header at lines 9-10 so it matches.

findings.line: 225-268 (in1, in2, in3, in6, in7) vs basisCases 383-474
findings.problem: Five of the 19 assertions have no red case. in1 (unknown key), in2 (10-character minimum counted after collapsing whitespace), in3 (500/501) and in6 (complete input: same entry, composed wording, collapsed note, 18+ recorded) never go red under any plant. in7 goes red only by accident, under the noPhoneScreen plant. They can fail in principle, but --prove-red never shows it. The caseFoldedLookup plant swaps only impl.lookup, while impl.check still calls the real consentBasisFor, so in1 is not exercised by it.
findings.fix: Add BasisDefect flags and cases, each expecting its own label. unknownDefaults: check maps an unknown key to OWN_FORM, expect in1. lengthBeforeNormalize: count raw.length, expect in2. maxOffByOne: reject only above 501, expect in3. noteStoredRaw: return the raw proofNote in the ok result, expect in6. oneSentence: every refusal says the same sentence, expect in7.

findings.problem: draft2 only sees one written shape of a writer. WORDING_WRITER needs the literal prefix `db.`, so a consent write inside commitBatch's ONE transaction (X3), such as `tx.messagingConsent.create(` or a new batch DAL member like `db.messagingConsent.appendMany(`, is invisible. The basis-writer arm uses `fixConsentBasis`, a name from the U33 spec that DECISIONS never fixed: X2/M4 put the basis write in U32's start action on U29's model, possibly via transition/update. NAMES_CATALOGUE matches only a direct specifier ending `consent-basis` or `consent-basis.ts`, so a re-export barrel or a `.js` specifier gets past it. Only the planted writer in the red cases proves the detector; the normal run has no positive control for it.
findings.fix: Widen WORDING_WRITER to /\b\w+\.messagingConsent\.(?:create|createMany)\b|\bfixConsentBasis\(|\brecordImportConsentBatch\(/. Also match `consent-basis(?:\.[cm]?[jt]s)?` and follow one re-export hop. Add a CONTROL inside assertConsentBasis that runs the detectors on a fixed planted source with a relative import and requires a hit. Keep the red case.

findings.problem: normalizeProofNote applies NFKC to the note that is stored, so seven-year ledger evidence is no longer the officer's text. Examples: '№4' becomes 'No4', '½' becomes '1⁄2', '™' becomes 'TM', and full-width CJK punctuation becomes ASCII. The doc comment at line 98 says the note is kept 'in the officer's words'. The fold is right for the phone screen, but not for the stored value.
findings.fix: Screen and count on a copy folded with NFKC and with Cf removed. Store and compose evidence from an NFC copy with only Cf removed and whitespace collapsed (e.g. normalizeProofNote returns { stored, screened }, or add a separate screen-only helper). Count the length on the stored form so the panel's live count and the server agree.

findings.problem: The comment at line 181 says the screen catches 'a phone number, however it is written', but NUMBER_SEPARATORS strips only whitespace, '.', brackets, '+' and dashes. '0712/345/678', '0712_345_678', '0712·345·678' and '0712,345,678' all pass into evidence. The spec's list of separators is met, but the claim is wider than the code.
findings.fix: Either reword the comment to name exactly the separators the spec lists, or strip any non-letter run between two digits, e.g. note.replace(/(?<=\p{Nd})[^\p{L}\p{Nd}]+(?=\p{Nd})/gu, ""). If you widen it, add those variants to in4's phones and recheck its notPhones list for false positives such as lists of stand numbers.

findings.problem: importConsentEvidence says 'NO NUMBER EVER' but does not check for one. A future caller that passes the raw request note, or a run row written by a buggy path, puts a phone number into unprunable seven-year evidence. runId is also unchecked: a runId containing ' basis:THIRD_PARTY' would make the one-line evidence parse ambiguously.
findings.fix: Make it total: return null (or throw) when holdsPhoneShapedRun(normalized note) is true or runId fails /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/. Add one ev sub-case asserting that a phone-bearing note composes nothing.

findings.problem: The header says '`test:client-graph-safe` pins it'. That is false until the lead adds the reported PINNED line, because the engineer correctly did not edit scripts/client-graph-safe.test.mjs. Under DECISIONS M10, client-graph-safe also stays out of predeploy until U29b, so the pin will not block a deploy yet.
findings.fix: Lead adds `"lib/marketing/consent-basis.ts",` with the reported comment after `"lib/marketing/footer.ts",` in scripts/client-graph-safe.test.mjs, in the same commit. Until then, reword the header to 'must be pinned in test:client-graph-safe (M3)'.

findings.problem: The comment markers don't follow the repo's convention. 🔴 marks a FOUND defect, but here it labels the G4 draft status: 'G4 · THE FOUR WORDINGS … ARE DRAFTS', 'G4 · Ali's confirmation', 'G4 DRAFT', 'G4 DRAFTS'. The 🔴 at line 15 (OD9's false premise) is correct.
findings.fix: Use ⚠️ (or ⛔ for 'nothing writes them') on the four G4 lines, and keep 🔴 for the OD9 finding.

review.verdict:
I found nothing critical or high; the code is safe to land once the lead makes two calls: the scope of U33.draft2 (medium) and adding the client-graph-safe pin. Nothing was run, by rule. What I checked by reading and by Python:
- **Pin:** PINNED_BASIS_SHA f9d9ac400b285144 recomputes exactly from the file's strings.
- **Wordings:** all five copy the spec drafts exactly.
- **Bytes:** neither new file has control, zero-width or no-break-space characters, and every regex escape (\p{..}, \d, \s, \[, \]) is intact. The runner is CRLF in the working tree only because autocrlf is on; HEAD is LF and git will normalise it.
- **Client safety:** consent-basis.ts imports nothing.
- **TypeScript:** I found no errors by reading. Target is ES2022, the \p{} classes carry the u flag, StoredMessagingConsent fits ImportAttestationRow, and the union narrowing in the .mts is sound.
- **Ownership:** only scripts/marketing-consent.test.mts was edited outside the new files, it is not on the do-not-edit list, and the diff is the U33a registration only. client-graph-safe and package.json were correctly left alone.
- **Decisions honoured:** G4 is enforced (CONSENT_BASIS_G4 is DRAFT, every since is 'unshipped'), C2 (unknown keys are refused), X5 (only cited), and there is no ledger UNKNOWN.
- **Red cases:** I traced all 18 plants and each one turns its own named assertion red; the model is faithful (§0b).
- **draft2 walk:** it covers 1,222 src files and finds 4 ledger writers (consent-ledger, optout-service, erase, the dev-test seed route), so its 1000 and 3 floors hold.
- **Runner wiring:** the 'basis case' tally prefix cannot collide with 'case'.

Remaining issues:
- **Medium:** draft2 blocks U33a's engine commit (critic step 8), and X3 makes that commit a prerequisite for U32. Ali is away, so the lead should choose and record the choice.
- **Low:**
  - five assertions have no red case (in1, in2, in3, in6, in7);
  - draft2's detector misses tx./new-DAL-member writers and re-exports;
  - NFKC rewrites the stored evidence note;
  - the phone-separator comment claims more than the code does;
  - importConsentEvidence does not check its own note or run id;
  - the header's 'pinned' claim depends on the lead's edit;
  - 🔴 is used on draft labels instead of found defects.
